text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Parliament will decide whether to ban Turkish citizens from going to casinos or to close gaming establishments all together.
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan will unveil a package for economic and social improvement in the impoverished and strife-ridden southeast by the end of December.
- Erbakan introduced a regulation limiting the powers of foreign minister Tansu Ciller -- his coalition partner.
- An opinion poll following a scandal over the state's links with the underworld reveals Turks' pessimism and suspicions.
- Environmental groups pledge the government's plans for Turkey's first nuclear plant will never be realised.
- State-owned Ziraat Bank plans is starting a programme to support agriculture with its own resources.
- Turkey and the United States will continue for another 10 days their talks on the status a U.S-led allied air force stationed in Turkey to protect Iraqi Kurds.
- A parliamentary commission investigating a security scandal has not been able to find documents relating to its probe.
